verses.1: And the LORD said to Moses, “Go, you and the people you have brought up from Egypt to the land that I have promised to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I will give it to your descendants.”
verses.2: And I sent forth an angel before you, and I conquered the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, and the Hivvites.
verses.3: To the land of milk and honey… For I will not enter it while you are still alive. You are a people who are stubborn and perverse. So, I will not eat you in that place.
verses.4: And the people heard these bad words. They became sad, and no one comforted them.
verses.5: And the LORD said to Moses, “To the children of Israel, you are a difficult people. For a moment, I will bring down your sins upon you. Now, I will take away your sins from you, and then I will know what I will do to you.”
verses.6: And the sons of Israel took their plowshares from Har-Horov.
verses.7: And Moses would take the tent and go to it, away from the camp. He would call it “the Tabernacle”. And everyone who sought God would come to the Tabernacle, which was located away from the camp.
verses.8: And when Moses left the tabernacle, all the people stood up and stood by the entrance of the tabernacle. They watched as Moses entered the tabernacle.
verses.9: And it shall be that when Moses enters the tabernacle, the cloud will descend, and the door of the tabernacle will be closed. Then God will speak to Moses.
verses.10: And all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tabernacle. Then all the people stood up and bowed down as one person opened the doors of the tabernacle.
verses.11: And the LORD spoke to Moses face to face, just as a person speaks to another. Then he returned to the camp. His servant was Joshua, a young man who had not yet reached adulthood.
verses.12: And Moses said to Jehovah, “See, you have said to me, ‘Take this people with you.’ But you do not know what you are sending me to do. You said that you knew what you was doing, and yet you still found favor in my eyes.”
verses.13: And now, if I have pleased you, then please tell me your ways. Let me know so that I can find pleasure in your eyes. And see that your people, this nation, are truly worthy of it.
verses.14: And he said, “Let my feet go, and I will leave you alone.”
verses.15: And he said to him, “If your face does not go with us, then let us leave you behind.”
verses.16: And in what way will Efoa know that I have earned your favor? I and my people will walk with you, and we will fall down before you. I and my people will be preferred over all the other nations that live on this land.
verses.17: And the LORD said to Moses, “I will do what you have said. For I have found your words pleasing in my eyes, and I will know you by your name.”
verses.18: And He said, “Please show me your glory.”
verses.19: And he said, “I will carry all my good things before your face. I will call upon the name of Jehovah before you. I will store up those who are righteous, and I will have mercy on those who are in need.”
verses.20: And he said, “You cannot see my face, for no man shall ever see my face.”
verses.21: And the LORD said, “Behold, I have given you a place where you can stand upon the rock.”
verses.22: And it shall be that in my time, I will lay you down on the ground, and I will rest my hands on you until I have finished my work.
verses.23: And I took off my head, and you saw my other side; but my face was not visible.
